dct_description_sm: First Nations are among the most vulnerable to the impacts of climate change, and will be faced with a number of challenges unparalleled by the non-aboriginal population due in large part to their geographic location, poor infrastructure and strong reliance on the natural environment. To date, considerable research has been compiled on the impacts of climate change on First Nations communities, as well as mitigation and adaptation efforts. Much of this research has focused on northern Aboriginal communities, with far less emphasis placed on First Nation communities south of sixty degrees latitude. It is in this capacity that the Environmental Stewardship Unit (ESU) of the Assembly of First Nations (AFN) undertook a climate change gap analysis. This analysis would provide an assessment of the current state of climate change adaptation efforts and programming in First Nations communities south of sixty degrees latitude, at the federal, provincial, regional and local levels.
